issue.title: PR mirror's incremental fetch_limit=200 over created-descending order hides the oldest PRs from every pass but the daily full scan
issue.description:
Deferred deliberately by epic sase-k2's plan (plans:202608/external_mirror_refinement.md, phase 'perf'): 'Do not widen the incremental fetch in this phase. fetch_limit=200 against gh pr list's created-descending order can miss an old PR that was just updated; that is a real gap, but it is a provider-ordering question that deserves its own task bead rather than a change smuggled into a performance phase.' Filed by sase-k2.land at close, as that plan directed.

MECHANISM (confirmed in source and in live run records): src/sase/external_mirror/pr_sync.py:78 defaults fetch_limit=200 and line 103 sets 'limit = 0 if full else fetch_limit', so only the daily DAILY_REPAIR_SCAN full pass lists the tracker unbounded. The provider seam exposes a record limit, not a page cursor, and gh pr list returns created-descending, so an incremental pass sees the 200 most recently CREATED PRs regardless of which PRs were most recently UPDATED.

LIVE EVIDENCE: gh_sase-org__sase has 296 PRs. Every external_pr_mirror[sase] run record under ~/.sase/axe/lumberjacks/external_mirror/chops/ on 2026-08-12 (14:10, 14:16, 14:31, 14:46) reports 'fetched': 200 with 'seen': 168 — the limit is saturated on every incremental pass, so roughly 96 of the oldest PRs are structurally invisible to the 15-minute cadence.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW: before epic sase-k2 an unseen old PR only delayed adoption. sase-k2.5 added the refresh action, so an already-adopted external Patch only follows its PR from open to merged/closed on a pass that actually fetches that PR. An old PR that merges today is therefore reconciled by the daily full scan rather than within one 15-minute tick — a bounded but real up-to-24h staleness window on Patch status and on the active-to-archive move, and the window scales with how far down the created-descending list the PR sits.

SCOPE: a provider-ordering question. Options worth weighing rather than assuming: teach the PR-listing seam to sort by updated-at (gh pr list --search 'sort:updated-desc' or equivalent) so the incremental window tracks the cursor's own dimension; expose real pagination on the seam; or raise/derive fetch_limit from the project's PR count. Whichever is chosen must keep the pass inside the external_mirror lane's 5-minute chop timeout and the existing per-pass create budget.

RELEVANT FILES: src/sase/external_mirror/pr_sync.py (fetch_limit, _candidate_in_window, OVERLAP_WINDOW, DAILY_REPAIR_SCAN), the vcs provider PR-listing seam, docs/axe.md 'Builtin external_pr_mirror'.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-kk — the issue-side twin of this gap from the same epic (sase-k2). Independent modules, no ordering constraint between them.

Triage sweep 2026-08-14 (requested by the project owner: keep the seven highest-impact open tasks, close the rest). Both are known, precisely-diagnosed mirror gaps filed by sase-k2.land: an already-closed upstream issue never fires a close transition (its state is seeded on the creating pass), and the PR mirror's incremental fetch_limit=200 over gh's created-descending order hides the oldest PRs from every pass but the DAILY_REPAIR_SCAN. Neither loses data -- the daily full scan is the backstop -- and neither has an independent reporter. sase-kl was already a deliberate deferral in epic sase-k2's plan. Re-file with a +1 if a stale mirrored bead actually misleads triage.

payload.close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: external-mirror fidelity gaps are self-correcting on the daily full scan and have no reported user impact.
